message: Ten rivers flow into this huge wetland! Close by, in Kuttanad, farmers grow rice below sea level, behind walls of clay, coir and bamboo that keep the salty water out.

field_find.name: Kuttanad's rice fields
field_find.note: Fields reclaimed from the lake by hand, named a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System in 2013.

alt: Bright green rice fields below the waterline, a canal and coconut palms along a clay bank.

sources.title: Vembanad-Kol Wetland, Ramsar Sites Information Service
sources.supports: Largest brackish wetland on India's southwest coast, fed by 10 rivers; coordinates

sources.title: FAO Heritage Status to Kuttanad, Kerala Tourism (Government of Kerala)
sources.supports: Farming below sea level; land reclaimed from Vembanad Lake; bunds of coir, bamboo and clay; FAO GIAHS status in 2013

review.notes: Kerala Tourism pages disagree on Kuttanad's depth below sea level, so the card gives no number.
